email.headline: Bledisloe Cup — Sydney Test
bodyParagraphs: Suaalii is back at centre and Meredith takes the reins: Sydney asks whether Australia's new connections can withstand New Zealand's pressure.

Australia have named Isaac Henry and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii in midfield, with Declan Meredith partnering Ryan Lonergan in the halves. Ben Donaldson is unavailable through injury. Harry Potter starts on the left wing; Lukhan Salakaia-Loto reaches his 50th Test. New Zealand have named George Bower, Fabian Holland and Josh Moorby to start, with Damian McKenzie at flyhalf and Beauden Barrett at fullback. These are announced selections, not projected combinations.

The aerial contest remains an important tactical question at Accor Stadium, but Suaalii's move inside changes where Australia deploy their threat. Potter, Jorgensen and Wright must connect the catch with the next phase while the midfield organises around them. New Zealand's McKenzie-Barrett combination offers decision-making across the backline. This is Australia's final home Test before the northern tour; announced substitutes include uncapped Harry McLaughlin-Phillips, whose appearance is not guaranteed. Stan Sport carries the match in Australia.

Meredith's familiar connection with Lonergan gives Australia's reshuffle one established reference point. Outside them, Henry and Suaalii must turn a changed midfield into a shared understanding under pressure. That is the substance behind a home crowd's hope: decisions made together, not an individual rescue act. Salakaia-Loto's milestone gives the occasion another personal thread, while the possibility of a McLaughlin-Phillips debut places a new beginning alongside that experience.
